verification_scope_reason: Actual Source runProfilePnpm and Native service operations invoke the same controlled executable over independent real profiles. Observe pre-install registry metadata/flags and refusal, expected name/version/bundle and extra/missing dependency rejection, unchanged versus replaced incompatible dependencies, bundle component and devDependency compatibility, original CRLF lock restoration versus absent lockfile, successful and failed repair requests, activation versus disabled activation, plain dependencies, unsupported Host activation without uninstalling dependencies, removal selection and numeric package-name enumeration. Result fields, diagnostics, callbacks, profile manifests, lock bytes and executable arguments compare exactly. Invalid recorded runs refuse before reading even a corrupt profile; stale records permit work. Additional Native tests validate malformed/boolean/unsafe/floating-integer run identities, bounded active refusal and natural process exit without terminating it, and dot-relative path anchoring. Oversized Node-invalid process ids are rejected before ctypes can truncate them. The 83 original Source operation cases all pass.
legal_adaptation: Service engine delegates process ownership and strengthened cancellation to C8-BU. The caller must already hold the canonical profile write lock. Repair has its own owned run record/log and the Source total repair deadline rather than a silence deadline. It completes before diagnostics report restoration; callback output from repair is not mixed into the installation stream. Controlled repair commands qualify invocation, waiting and returned outcomes, not acquisition or actual reinstalling of a real plugin tree.
activation_boundary: Shared captured service operation layer only. Canonical CLI inherited execution/initialization, manager Remote install/update/remove and build approval streams, and built-in Python registry/acquisition/install backend composition remain pending.
